bullets.text: BofA 2Q preview: Hindalco India EBITDA dips QoQ on lower LME aluminium; Novelis EBITDA/t resilient; Hindustan Zinc benefits from higher zinc.
bullets.source: BofA — India Insight: DMart | Consumer Preview | Metals & Mining | Oil & Gas | Cement | PI Inds | Financials | Economic Watch

detail.summary: BofA's metals preview sees 2Q earnings split by metal: aluminium price weakness weighs on Hindalco's domestic business, while zinc strength lifts Hindustan Zinc. Novelis is the offset at group level. This is a sales commentary summary, not full research.
points: Hindalco India EBITDA to fall QoQ on lower LME aluminium
Novelis adj. EBITDA/t seen resilient
Hindustan Zinc to benefit from higher zinc prices
Sector peers: Coal India EBITDA +2% QoQ, NMDC -25% QoQ

bullets.text: LME aluminium tested $3,040/t June low on 8-Oct; Chinese primary stocks rose 48kt to 686kt, capping rebound near $3,160-3,180.
bullets.source: Emkay — Base Metals Market Report: Aluminum – Weak price action meets rising Chinese stocks and dollar-side risks

detail.summary: Emkay sees aluminium under pressure from China's post-holiday restart, with social inventories building and downstream demand subdued. A technical bounce is possible if the June low holds, but fundamentals limit upside. Domestic MCX curve shows near-term backwardation despite weak outright price.
points: MCX aluminium -0.40% on week to Rs335.35/kg
China social stocks 686,000MT at 8-Oct; bonded 114,600MT
LME stocks 238,875MT; cash-3M contango about $15/MT
MCX first-second month backwardation Rs1.45/kg
UAE aluminium scrap export ban continues past 8-Oct review

bullets.text: India HRC at INR64,700/t, a four-year high, with spot margin ~INR39,110/t, up ~INR3,000 q-q; Nomura stays Buy on Tata, JSW, Jindal Steel.
bullets.source: Nomura — India steel - Steel weekly trends (week ended 09 Oct 2026)

detail.summary: Nomura argues price hikes already taken more than absorb raw-material inflation, so 1HFY27 earnings stay supported. Rebar is catching up with flat, narrowing the flat-long spread, while seaborne coking coal has started to ease from its spike.
points: HRC +INR700/t w-w; rebar +INR900/t w-w to INR63,800/t
Flat-long spread down to ~INR900/t
Coking coal -USD3/t w-w to USD271/t, ~3% below Sep average
Iron ore USD87/t CFR China, lowest of CY26
NMDC lumps +INR150/t to INR5,400/t from Sep-26

bullets.text: BofA expects steel EBITDA/t to contract q-q in 2Q on weaker long prices and higher coking coal; volume growth cushions.
bullets.source: BofA — India Insight: DMart | Consumer Preview | Metals & Mining | ... (12 Oct)

detail.summary: BofA's 2QFY27 metals preview is sales commentary, not research. It flags a margin squeeze per tonne for steel from long-product price weakness and coking coal costs, partly offset by higher volumes.
points: Steel EBITDA/t to fall q-q in 2QFY27
Drivers: weaker long steel prices, higher coking coal
Volume growth to cushion the impact
Adjacent: NMDC EBITDA seen -25% q-q

bullets.text: HRC-Patra spread widened 6.9% w-w to INR13,802/t vs 3-month average INR11,884; Nuvama calls it negative for low-end HRC pipe makers.
bullets.source: Nuvama — HRC-patra spread widens by 6.9% WoW to INR 13,802/ton (+1 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: HRC kept rising while Patra (the pipe-end price) slipped, so the spread over HRC is wider than its recent average. Nuvama sees the squeeze falling on HRC-based pipe manufacturers, especially in the low-end segment.
points: HRC +0.9% w-w to INR64,994/t
Patra -0.6% w-w to INR51,193/t
Spread INR13,802/t vs 3-month average INR11,884/t
HRC and Patra both up 14% over three months

bullets.text: Nomura: cement needs INR12-15/bag hikes to offset petcoke at USD184/t (+25% q-q); only INR10/bag announced for Oct. Top picks UltraTech, Dalmia.
bullets.source: Nomura — India cement - Fuel cost inflation raises the pricing hurdle

detail.summary: Fuel inflation has intensified after 2QFY27 but lags the P&L by 60-90 days, so the bulk hits 4QFY27. Hikes must be absorbed in October, before the festive slowdown limits pricing. Spreads are manageable for now but could narrow if hikes fail to stick.
points: Imported petcoke USD184/t, +25% q-q in Oct'26
Required hikes ~INR12-15/bag post-GST
INR10/bag hikes announced for Oct'26
Cement spread INR2,492/t, 3% below 2-year average
Cost pressure mostly 4QFY27F, limited in 3QFY27F

bullets.text: BofA: cement cost pressure extends into 3Q, not peaking in 2Q as assumed; FY27 estimates revised, 2Q prices flattish. Buy UltraTech.
bullets.source: BofA — India Insight: DMart | Consumer Preview | Metals & Mining | Oil & Gas | Cement | PI Inds | Financials | Economic Watch

detail.summary: Sales-commentary blurb ahead of 2Q results. Demand is healthy on a low base and below-average monsoon, but West Asia uncertainty keeps costs elevated. The focus is on whether recent price hikes stick enough to offset cost pressure.
points: 2Q demand momentum similar to 1Q
Cost peak now seen in 3Q vs 2Q earlier
Pan-India prices flattish in 2Q
FY27 estimates revised
Buy rating on UltraTech

bullets.text: BofA 2QFY27 preview: NMDC EBITDA to fall 25% QoQ; Coal India EBITDA +2% as higher e-auction premiums offset seasonal volume dip.
bullets.source: BofA — India Insight: DMart | Consumer Preview | Metals & Mining | Oil & Gas | Cement | PI Inds | Financials | Economic Watch

detail.summary: BofA's Metals & Mining preview sets up a split between the two PSU miners for the quarter. Coal India's pricing mix (auction premiums) outweighs a seasonal volume dip, while NMDC is expected to see a sharp sequential earnings decline.
points: NMDC EBITDA expected to fall 25% QoQ
Coal India EBITDA expected to rise 2% QoQ
Driver: higher e-auction premiums
Offset: seasonal volume dip
Part of wider M&M preview, 2QFY27E

bullets.text: Adani's Kutch Copper plans to double smelting capacity to 1 million tonnes, per Kotak's daily news list.
bullets.source: Kotak — Basic materials - daily news and prices

bullets.text: Zetwerk IPO prices at INR143-151, ~US$519mn at upper end (INR28.3bn fresh, INR21.8bn OFS); books open 15 Oct, close 19 Oct.
bullets.source: Kotak — ***KOTAK DEAL: IPO of Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses Limited - Pre-Anchor Announcement***

detail.summary: Kotak's pre-anchor announcement sets the Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses IPO terms. Upper-end post-money market cap is about US$2.8bn on fully diluted shares. Proceeds go largely to debt repayment at the company and subsidiaries, with the rest for acquisitions and general purposes.
points: Offer INR50,123mn (US$518.8mn) at upper end
Fresh INR28,300mn; OFS INR21,823mn
Mcap INR269,749mn fully diluted (US$2.79bn)
Anchor 14 Oct; open 15 Oct; close 19 Oct
Offer 18.6% of FDSO; QIB not less than 75%

bullets.text: Festive e-com GMV fell 7-10% YoY to Rs29,800-30,900cr over 7-10 Oct; premium phones above Rs45,000 resilient as smartphone prices rose 35-40%.
bullets.source: Nomura — India Consumer Durables and EMS: Festive online sales off to fine 'premium' start

detail.summary: Memory-chip-driven price inflation is hurting mass-market electronics volumes while premium holds up. Reports conflict on festive growth, with ET citing up to 40% premium growth and Datum showing GMV down year on year. Relevant to Dixon and Amber demand read-through.
points: GMV Rs29,800-30,900cr vs Rs33,200cr last year (Datum)
Mobile volumes -12% overall (Counterpoint)
Laptops and TVs up to 25% costlier
Mobile sales growth seen 6% vs 26% in 2025
Flipkart large appliances +30% YoY in first hour

bullets.text: HCLT 2QFY27: EBIT margin 18.2% beat, revenue missed on software (-5.8% qoq); FY27 growth guide narrowed to 2.5-4% (from 1-4%), implying weak 2H.
bullets.source: PhillipCapital — HCL Technologies (HCLT IN) - Mixed results; Narrowed Guidance band implies weak H2 (+Kotak, JPM, MS, CLSA first takes)

detail.summary: Services grew 3.0% qoq CC but software fell on fewer multi-year renewals. Margin beat came from efficiencies, advanced AI mix, SG&A leverage and FX. The narrower guide implies ~1% 2H services CQGR as the mega deal only ramps in 1QFY28.
points: Revenue $3,724mn, +2.3% qoq CC; EBIT margin 18.2%, +131bps
Software -5.8% qoq CC; Kotak: ARR +2.6% organic
Advanced AI $219mn, +28% qoq, 5.9% of revenue
TCV $3.26bn, +35% qoq incl. $1.14bn mega deal
EBIT margin guide held at 17.5-18.5%

bullets.text: HCLT targets: PhillipCapital cuts to Rs1,290 from 1,430 (Neutral); Kotak FV Rs1,220 REDUCE; Emkay ADD Rs1,250; Avendus REDUCE Rs1,280; CMP Rs1,223.
bullets.source: Kotak — [Kotak] HCL Technologies (CMP: Rs1,223, FV: Rs1,220, REDUCE): Margins surprise, products disappoint, valuations full

detail.summary: Houses agree the quarter was mixed and valuation is full, so ratings stay put. Phillip lowers its multiple to 17x from 18x and trims FY27-28 EPS 1-2%. Kotak raises margins, lifting FY28-29 EPS 0.1-1% and FV on roll-forward at an unchanged 15x.
points: Phillip: TP Rs1,290 (was 1,430), FY27E EPS Rs74.1, -1.0%
Kotak: FV Rs1,220 (was 1,200), 16x FY28E EPS
Emkay ADD Rs1,250; Avendus REDUCE Rs1,280 (headline ratings)
Phillip 52-wk range Rs1,030-1,780

bullets.text: MS CIO survey: 2026 IT services budget growth 2.0% (from 1.8%), 2027 stable at 2%; slight positive for India IT, no near-term catalysts. (+10 more in Outlook)
bullets.source: Morgan Stanley — India Technology: 3Q26 CIO Survey: IT Services: Stable 2027 Budget Expectations

detail.summary: Overall IT budgets edged up, led by the US and offset by Europe. MS reads Accenture results plus the survey as stable-to-slightly-decelerating services spend next year. Without acceleration in FY28 revenue growth, India IT forecasts and multiples remain at risk.
points: 2026 IT budget growth +4.0%, +23bps qoq; 2027 stable +4.0%
Services 2027 spend +2% yoy; Financials and Energy strongest
26% of CIOs fund AI from net-new budget (33% in 2Q26)
64% plan to buy AI capabilities vs 17% build

bullets.text: UBS expects 75bp of RBI hikes to 6% repo after September CPI hit 5.5% (food 7.7%); headline stays above 5.5% for three quarters.
bullets.source: UBS — India Economic Comment "September CPI inflation climbs to 5.5%, with..."

detail.summary: Inflation is broadening beyond food, with core and rural prices firming. Real policy rates turn negative as CPI stays well above the 4% target, forcing a monetary recalibration. El Nino effects on global food prices lag 6-18 months, adding 2027 upside risk.
points: Headline CPI 5.5% vs 4.8% in August
Food 7.7% vs 6.0%; vegetables & pulses 9.2%
Core 4.3% vs 4.1%; rural 6.1%, urban 4.9%
FY27 CPI avg 5.2%; above 5% through 1H FY28
Cumulative 75bp hikes take repo to 6%

bullets.text: RBI lifts daily CRR maintenance to 99%, adds Rs250bn OMO sale and OMC dollar window; CLSA sees INR toward 95 from 96.70, 10-year yield breaking 7.30%.
bullets.source: CLSA — India economics: More liquidity and FX measures

detail.summary: The weekend measures drain liquidity and cut dollar demand, supporting the rupee near term. CLSA calls them a band-aid, with focus returning to crude, FX flows and the FY28 BoP after a few weeks, and more liquidity steps possible including a CRR hike.
points: CRR maintenance 90% to 99% from 16 October
20% FERR on importer hedges above US$2m
Non-underlying FX derivative limit cut to US$5m from US$100m
FX reserves US$735bn vs US$786bn early-September peak
97/US$ possibly the unofficial RBI red line

bullets.text: Kotak sees Nifty-50 2QFY27 net profit +21% yoy, FY27 EPS Rs1,227; downgrades IT, 4W autos and chemicals, upgrades 2W, private banks, pharma. (+14 more in Outlook)
bullets.source: Kotak — Kotak Q2 Earnings preview - Strong quarter.

detail.summary: Kotak's sector preview summary flags a strong quarter led by pharma, EMS, private banks and 2W, while ferrous metals, large-cap IT and agri-inputs are weak. Metals preference leans ferrous over non-ferrous given macro backdrop and dollar strength.
points: KIE universe net income +21% yoy
Metals: top BUYs Jindal Steel, JSW Steel, Vedanta Aluminium
Weak prints: Tata Steel, Wipro, Infosys, Maruti, Hyundai
EMS strong: Syrma, Avalon, Cyient DLM; Kaynes weak
Staples margins pressured; ITC, Asian Paints weak

bullets.text: JPM: Reliance O2C EBITDA seen +24% QoQ to Rs210bn on diesel exports; SAED-exempt SEZ refinery; stays O/W.
bullets.source: JPM — India Oil and Gas: Net Diesel cracks - why Indian refiners should have a better 2Q

detail.summary: Indian refiners do not capture the full diesel crack because of the SAED, and net cracks have fallen back to May lows on freight. Even so, September-quarter net cracks are up sharply on June-Q, and higher diesel exports and lower LPG output support Q2 margins.
points: O2C EBITDA Rs170bn to Rs210bn QoQ, c.24%
Reliance SEZ refinery exempt from SAED
Diesel exports up in July/Aug vs 1Q (PPAC)
LPG output down despite steady refinery throughput
Prefers MAHGL (N) over IGL (U/W); CGD margin risk

bullets.text: CLSA: Nifty Auto down c.17% in two months; M&M at c.15x FY28 core EPS, HC O-PF maintained.
bullets.source: CLSA — India Research - Gravita, DMart, IRB Infra, India Recycling, Autos, IT... (India autos: Right here, right now)

detail.summary: The sell-off reflects commodity-inflation margin fears, price-hike demand worries and de-rating after the GST-cut rebase, while retail demand stays robust. CLSA argues the GST growth rebase is neither new nor unexpected, so risk-reward now looks attractive even on conservative FY28 assumptions.
points: Nifty Auto -c.17% over two months
OEMs reiterated mid-to-high single-digit 2HFY27 growth
M&M c.15x FY28CL core EPS
Assumes 10% tractor decline in FY28
c.10% EPS CAGR in conservative case; target unchanged

ai_semis.text: US semis sold off: SOX -2.7%, Ciena and Lumentum -10% on AI-spend caution; Broadcom CEO flagged financing as a bigger AI bottleneck than components.
ai_semis.source: JPM — JPM | Views on Asia Tech

ai_semis.text: JPM stays bullish AI: sees big-5 US cloud capex +67% to $1.21tr in 2027 and +22% to $1.48tr in 2028; hyperscaler ROI above 30%.
ai_semis.source: JPM — JPM | Views on Asia Tech

ai_semis.text: JPM Asia tech feedback: investors positive on substrates/packaging (Ibiden, ASE, TSMC), cautious on HBM chain (Hanmi, ASMPT, BESI); Micron -4% on CXMT competition.
ai_semis.source: JPM — JPM | Views on Asia Tech
